record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Let T ⊆ 2^{<ω} be a positive tree, meaning that [T] has positive measure. Let P^− be the statement that every positive tree has infinitely many distinct paths, and let P be the statement that every positive tree has a perfect subtree. Over RCA_0, does P^− imply P?

evidence.quote: A tree T ⊆ 2<ω is positive if [T] has measure > 0. Consider the following statements: ... P: For every positive tree T, there is a subtree S ⊆ T which is perfect. P−: For every positive tree there are distinct (Xn : n ∈ ω) such that Xn ∈ [T].
Problem 10. Is it true that RCA0 ⊢ P− → P?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the language of second-order arithmetic. Identify elements of $2^{<\omega}$ with finite binary strings, and let $[T] \subseteq 2^{\omega}$ denote the set of infinite paths through a tree $T \subseteq 2^{<\omega}$ (i.e., the set of $X \in 2^{\omega}$ all of whose finite initial segments lie in $T$). Equip $2^{\omega}$ with the standard fair-coin product (Lebesgue) measure $\mu$. Call a tree $T \subseteq 2^{<\omega}$ positive if $\mu([T]) > 0$. A tree $S \subseteq 2^{<\omega}$ is perfect if every $\sigma \in S$ has two incomparable extensions $\tau_0, \tau_1 \in S$.

Consider the following two principles:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathsf{P}$: Every positive tree $T \subseteq 2^{<\omega}$ has a perfect subtree $S \subseteq T$.
\item $\mathsf{P}^{-}$: For every positive tree $T \subseteq 2^{<\omega}$ there exists a sequence $(X_n)_{n \in \omega}$ of pairwise distinct elements of $[T]$.
\end{itemize}

Question: Does $\mathsf{RCA}_0 \vdash \mathsf{P}^{-} \to \mathsf{P}$? That is, working over the base system $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ of recursive comprehension, does the principle $\mathsf{P}^{-}$ imply the principle $\mathsf{P}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The principles P, P⁻, and P⁺ for positive trees have been studied as compactness-style principles between WKL and WWKL in reverse mathematics. The implication P⁻ → P over RCA₀ does not appear to be settled in the literature found; the question is listed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory. No published proof or refutation was located.

status_evidence.title: Pathwise-randomness and models of second-order arithmetic
status_evidence.snippet: Three principles between WKL and WWKL: every positive tree has a positive perfect subtree, a perfect subtree, and an infinite countable family of paths (P+, P, P-).
status_evidence.claim: The principles P, P⁻, P⁺ are studied in reverse mathematics but the implication P⁻ → P over RCA₀ is not established there.
